summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer was readmitted three days after prior discharge for intractable nausea and vomiting. She presented with over 20 episodes of non-bloody, brown emesis and was found to have hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and sinus tachycardia. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, potassium repletion, and antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, and lorazepam. Her blood pressure was controlled with IV metoprolol and transitioned to oral lisinopril. Gastric emptying study and upper GI with small bowel follow-through were normal, suggesting her symptoms were not due to motility or structural issues. Chronic microcytic anemia was identified, and iron supplementation was started. Due to recurrent symptoms without organic cause, outpatient brain MRI and psychiatric evaluation were recommended. Her diet was advanced to full, and she remained vomiting-free for two days prior to discharge. She was discharged home on her home medications with the addition of nightly lorazepam for nausea and anxiety.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
